subject: Stability incident — RCA summary & implementation commitments
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Kosinski <julia.kosinski@clearbay.com>
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Stability incident — initial findings and next steps

Hi Julia,

Thanks again for taking the time earlier. I wanted to follow up with an initial, concise summary of what we found from our preliminary investigation into the Aug 27 stability event that impacted ClearBay. We're sharing the findings now so your engineering and compliance teams can triage internally while we finish the full RCA.

Key points (high level):
- Trigger: a rare KV-cache eviction cascade when a batch of long-sequence requests caused unexpected memory pressure on a subset of inference nodes.
- Impact window: ~14:23–14:48 UTC on 2027-08-27; affected about 3% of your traffic, primarily long-chat sessions (>2k tokens).
- Observable effects: token-level delays and a small number of session resets; no data exposure detected.

Immediate actions we took:
- Isolated the pool and applied a temporary cache cap to prevent further cascade events.
- Rolled out a hotfix to improve eviction prioritization for long sequences.
- Enabled enhanced tracing for the affected pool to capture post-event behaviors.

Deliverables attached: a short RC A summary PDF, an event timeline CSV, and a tracker of implementation owners. We'll send the full technical RCA (with logs and mitigations) by EOD Wednesday.

Next steps for ClearBay: please confirm whether you'd like a dedicated sync with our on-call and your infra team to review logs (we can do a 45-minute session). Suggested times: Tue 30 Aug or Wed 31 Aug between 10:00–15:00 PT.

Appreciate your patience — we'll own the follow-up and make sure deadlines are clear.

Regards,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, rachel.kim@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 31 Aug 2027 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Stability incident — RCA summary & implementation commitments

Hi Julia and team,

Please find attached the full RCA summary and an owners tracker. This message synthesizes the key technical findings, timelines, and our commitments for remediation and verification.

Executive summary (concise):
- Root cause: an interaction between our dynamic KV-cache eviction policy and a previously unseen request distribution of long-sequence streaming sessions. The eviction algorithm prioritized short-lived prefixes during bursts, which led to repeated cache misses for long sessions and a cascading increase in CPU/latency as those sessions retried.
- Severity: operational impact limited to latency and a low rate of session resets; no integrity or exfiltration events detected after forensic review.
- Why it escaped detection: telemetry didn't include sequence-length-based sampling for that cluster; aggregated metrics looked healthy until the cascade threshold was reached.

Timeline (high level):
- 2027-08-27 14:23 UTC — first latency spike alerted via our synthetic monitors.
- 2027-08-27 14:28 UTC — increased error-rate and session resets observed in the affected pool.
- 2027-08-27 14:31–14:45 UTC — mitigation: temporary cache-cap applied; traffic routed away from the hot nodes.
- 2027-08-27 14:48 UTC — traffic normalizes; monitoring shows steady state.

Action items & commitments (owners + target dates):
- Implement deterministic eviction profiling for long-sequence sessions — Owner: Hannah Schmitt (hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai) — Target: 2027-09-10
- Add sequence-length-based telemetry and alerting for all production inference pools — Owner: Grace O'Connor (grace.oconnor@redwood.ai) — Target: 2027-09-07
- Backfill session traces for the event and share sanitized logs for your auditors — Owner: Rachel Kim (rachel.kim@redwood.ai) — Target: 2027-09-03
- Documentation & runbook update (incl. recommended client-side session sizing guidance) — Owner: Dylan Brooks — Target: 2027-09-14

Attachments: rca-summary-2027-08-27.pdf (includes detailed logs and mitigations), event-timeline-20270827.csv, implementation-owners-20270901.xlsx

Verification plan:
- Once owners deliver code/telemetry changes, Redwood will run a joint validation test with ClearBay traffic patterns in a controlled window and provide monitoring dashboards for acceptance.

We take this seriously and will provide weekly updates until commitments are complete. If you want the team to prioritize any single item for audit purposes, flag it and we'll accelerate.

Regards,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the thorough RCA and the clear owners list — that is exactly what we needed for our audit trail. A few follow-ups from our side before the validation run:

1) Can you share the sanitized traces (as noted) by EOD Friday 2027-09-03? Our compliance team will need them for the evidence bundle.
2) For the joint validation test: propose Sep 13 09:00 PT — Sep 13 11:00 PT. Please confirm whether your team can provision a validation window and the point of contact for the runbook.
3) We may request a short one-page statement confirming no data exposure occurred during the event for our board packet. If you can provide that by Sep 6, it would help speed our internal approvals.

We appreciate the weekly updates cadence. Please mark the items above as high priority.

Best,
Julia
Head of Platform Engineering, ClearBay
